policy_name: NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 & NSA CNSA Suite IPsec Guidance

rules.title: Deprecated Cipher (DES/3DES)
rules.description: DES and 3DES encryption algorithms are cryptographically broken and vulnerable to Sweet32 and key search attacks.
rules.impact: Confidentiality breach; complete traffic decryption by adversaries.
rules.recommendation: Immediately migrate to AES-256-GCM or AES-128-GCM.

rules.title: Acceptable 128-bit Encryption (AES-128)
rules.description: AES-128 provides adequate protection for standard enterprise communications but does not meet Top Secret CNSA 2.0 standards.
rules.impact: Lower security margin against future quantum/cryptanalytic advancements.
rules.recommendation: Upgrade to AES-256-GCM for high-assurance or government deployments.

rules.title: Weak Integrity Hash Algorithm (MD5/SHA-1)
rules.description: MD5 and SHA-1 suffer from severe collision vulnerabilities.

rules.title: Weak Diffie-Hellman Group (< 2048-bit)
rules.description: Diffie-Hellman Groups 1, 2, and 5 use modulus lengths below 2048 bits.
rules.impact: Key exchange eavesdropping via discrete logarithm computation.
rules.recommendation: Use DH Group 14 (2048-bit), Group 15 (3072-bit), or ECP Group 19 (256-bit).

rules.title: Legacy Diffie-Hellman Group 14 (2048-bit)
rules.description: DH Group 14 provides 112-bit security level, which is being phased out for high-security applications.
rules.recommendation: Upgrade to DH Group 15 (3072-bit MODP) or Group 19 (NIST P-256).

rules.title: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) Disabled
rules.description: Without PFS, compromise of long-term IKE private keys exposes all historical ESP sessions to retroactive decryption.
rules.impact: Historical session decryption if static keys are compromised.
rules.recommendation: Enable PFS on Child SA negotiations using DH Group 14 or higher.
